title: Flow Cytometry: Size Forward, Stuff Sideways
summary: Learn what forward and side scatter measure, how a CD45-versus-side-scatter plot isolates blasts, which markers assign lineage, why the diagnostic blast percentage comes from morphology, and how therapies erase gating markers.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 35 Hit 1 (core: FSC/SSC; CD45 vs SSC gate), Hit 2 (MPO, cytoplasmic CD3 lineage markers), Hit 3 (blast % from morphology), Hit 8 (therapy erases gating markers), Traps 1–2 and the Figure 35 anchor. Checked against Holl 2025, Ally & Chen 2024, Fuda & Chen 2025, Gajzer & Fromm 2025, Shameli 2025 and Lamble 2025. Context added: genetically defined AML exceptions to the 20% threshold (WHO-HAEM5/ICC). Pending: hemodilution/RBC-lysis explanation of flow vs morphology discrepancy.

objectives: Explain forward scatter, side scatter and fluorescent antibody detection.
Use a CD45-versus-side-scatter plot to locate blasts and name markers that assign lineage.
Explain why morphology supplies the diagnostic blast count and how targeted therapies affect gating.

scenes.title: Flow says 25% blasts — the smear says 12%
scenes.altText: A bone marrow from a patient with suspected acute leukaemia. The flow cytometry report says 25% blasts; the morphologic 500-cell differential says 12%. Which number decides the diagnosis — and what is flow actually good at?

cues.text: A marrow sample from a patient with suspected acute leukaemia goes to flow cytometry. The report says 25 percent blasts.
But the 500-cell count on the smear says 12 percent.
Which number counts? To answer, you need to know what flow measures — and what it doesn’t.

scenes.title: Normal: cells in single file past a laser
scenes.altText: Cells flow in single file through a laser beam. Light scattered forward (forward scatter, FSC) reflects cell size; light scattered to the side (side scatter, SSC) reflects internal complexity or granularity. Cells are also stained with fluorescent antibodies against CD markers; detectors measure each colour, so every cell gets a size, a granularity and a marker profile.

cues.text: In a flow cytometer, cells stream in single file through a laser beam, one at a time.
Light scattered forward tells you about size. Light scattered to the side tells you about what’s inside — granules and complexity.
The cells are also stained with antibodies carrying fluorescent dyes, each aimed at a CD marker.
Detectors read every colour, so each cell gets a size, a granularity and a list of markers — thousands of cells per second.

scenes.title: What changes: CD45 vs side scatter finds the blasts
scenes.altText: A schematic CD45 (x) vs side scatter (y) plot. Lymphocytes: bright CD45, low SSC. Monocytes: bright CD45, intermediate SSC. Granulocytes: moderate CD45, high SSC. Blasts: dim CD45, low SSC — the blast gate. The gated blasts are then tested for lineage: myeloperoxidase (MPO) for myeloid; cytoplasmic CD3 for T lineage; B-lineage markers such as CD19 with CD79a or CD22.

cues.text: The standard first picture plots CD45, the common white-cell marker, against side scatter. Normal populations land in familiar places.
Lymphocytes: bright CD45, little side scatter. Monocytes: bright CD45, a bit more. Granulocytes: high side scatter.
Blasts sit in their own corner: dim CD45 and low side scatter. Draw a gate there, and you’ve isolated the blasts.
Then ask what lineage they are. Myeloperoxidase points to myeloid; cytoplasmic CD3 to T cells; B-cell markers such as CD19 with CD79a or CD22 to B cells.

scenes.title: In the lab: what flow can’t decide alone
scenes.altText: Card 1: the blast percentage used to classify acute leukaemia comes from the morphologic count (e.g. ≥ 20% for acute leukaemias of ambiguous lineage); flow percentages are reported but don’t replace it. Note: some genetically defined AML types are diagnosed below 20% (WHO-HAEM5: no threshold for several; ICC: ≥ 10%). Card 2: therapy erases markers — rituximab removes detectable CD20; blinatumomab and CD19 CAR T reduce CD19; daratumumab blocks CD38 detection. Laboratories gate with other markers (e.g. CD22, CD79a/b, CD40/HLA-DR for B cells; CD319, CD138 for plasma cells).

cues.text: Back to the first question. The blast percentage that classifies an acute leukaemia comes from the morphologic count on the smear. Flow adds lineage and phenotype, but its percentage doesn’t replace that count.
There are exceptions in the other direction: some genetically defined AMLs are diagnosed even below 20 percent blasts.
Treatment can also erase the markers flow relies on. Rituximab removes detectable CD20. Blinatumomab and CD19 CAR T cells reduce CD19. Daratumumab blocks CD38.
So a “missing” B cell or plasma cell may just be wearing a different label. Labs gate with other markers — like CD22 or CD79 for B cells, and CD319 or CD138 for plasma cells.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Trap card: “Flow shows 25% blasts, so it’s AML” is crossed out → “Use the morphologic blast count (with genetic exceptions).” Trap card: “No CD20+ cells after rituximab = no B cells” is crossed out → “Gate B cells on CD19/CD22/CD79.” Trap card: “Bright side scatter = blasts” is crossed out → “Blasts are dim CD45, LOW side scatter.”

cues.text: Trap one: a flow blast percentage doesn’t establish the diagnosis. The morphologic count does — with some genetic exceptions.
Trap two: no CD20-positive cells after rituximab doesn’t mean no B cells. Look with other B-cell markers.
Trap three: blasts are not the high side-scatter cells. They’re dim CD45 with low side scatter.

scenes.title: Size forward, stuff sideways
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Forward = size, Side = stuff inside.” And “Blasts live in the dim, quiet corner (dim CD45, low SSC).” A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: forward is size, side is stuff inside. Blasts live in the dim, quiet corner — dim CD45, low side scatter.

Where it breaks: some leukaemias sit outside the classic blast gate — promyelocytes in APL have high side scatter; scatter depends on instrument settings; and lineage rules use intensity thresholds that differ between WHO and ICC.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “FSC = size, SSC = granularity; CD45 vs SSC gates blasts (dim CD45, low SSC)”, “Lineage: MPO, cytoplasmic CD3, B markers — blast % from morphology; therapy can erase markers”.

cues.text: Forward scatter is size and side scatter is granularity; CD45 versus side scatter finds the blasts, MPO and cytoplasmic CD3 assign lineage, morphology supplies the blast percentage, and treatment can erase the markers you gate on.

props.label: FSC = size · SSC = granularity · blasts = dim CD45, low SSC
MPO / cCD3 / B markers · blast % from morphology · therapy erases markers

explanation.what: Plain language: a flow cytometer looks at cells one by one, measuring size, inner graininess and which labelled markers they carry. Scientific terms: forward scatter (FSC) correlates with size, side scatter (SSC) with granularity/complexity; fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies identify CD antigens; CD45 vs SSC separates lymphocytes, monocytes, granulocytes and blasts.
explanation.why: Blasts express less CD45 and have few granules, placing them in a dim-CD45, low-SSC region; lineage-defining markers (MPO, cytoplasmic CD3, B-lineage markers) assign lineage. Targeted antibodies bind or remove their antigens, so the same epitopes cannot be detected by diagnostic reagents.
explanation.measure: Gating sequence: acquisition stability → singlets → viability → CD45 vs SSC → blast gate → lineage panel. Blast percentage for classifying acute leukaemia comes from morphologic evaluation (e.g. ≥ 20% for acute leukaemia of ambiguous lineage); several genetically defined AMLs are diagnosed without the 20% threshold (WHO-HAEM5) or at ≥ 10% (ICC). Post-therapy: rituximab (CD20), blinatumomab/CD19 CAR T (CD19), daratumumab (CD38) → gate with CD22, CD79a/b, CD40/HLA-DR (B cells) or CD319/CD138 (plasma cells).
explanation.differs: Scatter (physical properties) vs fluorescence (antigens); lymphocytes (bright CD45, low SSC) vs granulocytes (high SSC) vs blasts (dim CD45, low SSC); flow percentage vs morphologic blast count.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: FSC/SSC meaning, CD45 vs SSC as the first gate, MPO and cytoplasmic CD3 as lineage markers, morphology for blast percentage, and rituximab/daratumumab erasing markers.

questions.stem: On a CD45 versus side scatter plot of marrow, where do blasts typically fall?

options.rationale: Correct. Blasts express less CD45 than mature leukocytes and have few granules.
Incorrect. That is the lymphocyte region.
Incorrect. That is the granulocyte region.
Incorrect. That does not describe typical blasts.

questions.stem: Flow cytometry reports 28% blasts, but the 500-cell morphologic differential shows 12% blasts and cytogenetics show no defining abnormality. How should the blast percentage be used?

options.text: Use the morphologic count for classification; flow percentages do not replace it
options.rationale: Correct. Classification criteria specify a morphologic blast count.
Incorrect. The flow percentage is not the classifying count.
Incorrect. Averaging different methods is not valid.
Incorrect. The methods measure differently; morphology classifies.

questions.stem: A patient treated with rituximab has no CD20-positive cells on flow cytometry. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: CD20 may be undetectable because of therapy; look for B cells with CD19, CD22 or CD79
options.rationale: Correct. Rituximab removes detectable CD20, so other B-lineage markers must be used.

options.text: B cells are absent; disease is eradicated
options.rationale: Incorrect. Residual B cells may simply lack detectable CD20.

options.text: The sample is a T-cell lymphoma
options.rationale: Incorrect. Missing CD20 does not indicate T lineage.

options.text: Use CD38 to find B cells
options.rationale: Incorrect. CD38 is not a B-lineage marker.

claims.text: FSC ≈ size; SSC ≈ granularity; fluorescent antibodies detect CD markers.
CD45 vs SSC: blasts dim CD45/low SSC; lymphocytes bright CD45/low SSC; granulocytes high SSC.
MPO (myeloid), cytoplasmic CD3 (T), B markers (CD19 with CD79a/CD22) assign lineage.
Classifying blast % from morphology; genetic AML exceptions (WHO-HAEM5 no threshold; ICC ≥ 10%).
Rituximab (CD20), blinatumomab/CAR T (CD19), daratumumab (CD38) erase markers; alternative gating markers.
Flow blast counts are falsely low with hemodilution and falsely high after RBC lysis removes erythroid precursors.
